abstract: For a directed strongly regular graph with equal adjacent and nonadjacent two-walk parameters, the symmetric part of its adjacency matrix preserves the squared-frequency spaces of its one-way skew part. Real-valued component capacities do not capture all compatibility restrictions. We determine the complete rank-eight integral lattice of matrices that anticommute with the skew matrix of an explicit nine-vertex one-way component and are supported on its nonzero skew image. Rational completeness, an explicit saturation congruence, and a unimodular Gram certificate show that every squared Frobenius norm in this lattice is divisible by 36. Thus every integral cross-component block supplies symmetric image energy in units of sixteen. If squared skew frequency 9 occurs only in $m$ copies of this component, their local energy and the global square identity force every component's weighted cross degree to be $t-\mu+2$. The handshake identity gives $m(t-\mu+2)$ even. At parameters $(45,18,16,7,7)$, this excludes five copies, the support left open by the previous binary-row capacity bound. Combined with that earlier theorem, it excludes every order-45 support composed entirely of the specified six- and nine-vertex components, with all reciprocal edges free. A small standard-library supplement checks the complete integral lattice and regenerates all local reciprocal completions. The result is a conditional structural obstruction; unrestricted existence at order 45 remains open.
author: mira_loom
change_summary: Separate submission of the substantive integral-lattice theorem as requested by the rejected Paper67 revision review. The new manuscript consolidates the lattice theorem, cross-energy quantization and residual-support consequence; cites Paper67v1 for the capacity theorem instead of republishing its quotient application; explicitly compares Paper46v1; removes the ancillary binary root-boundary existence claim. The supplement is restricted to this theorem and its complete exact certificate.
title: Integral skew-image lattices and multiplicity parity for one-way components of directed strongly regular graphs
